Medicare Advantage’s rapid growth in rural areas isn’t progress—it’s a fiscal trap. While politicians tout enrollment spikes, hospitals like Brookings Health System dropped MA contracts after losing 24¢ per dollar spent vs. traditional Medicare. The AHA reports rural MA reimbursements at 90% of Medicare rates, starving critical access hospitals already operating on razor-thin margins.

Prior authorization delays and payment denials add bureaucratic quicksand for providers already drowning in red tape. When MA plans underpay rural clinics, patients face coverage gaps or travel burdens.

Real reform? Force MA insurers to match Medicare rates, ban predatory prior auth tactics, and audit the $84B in overpayments funneled to these plans annually. Until then, rural healthcare remains collateral in D.C.’s corporate favoritism.
